info.name: Lab - Video Kiosk
info.description: In this lab, we learn how to transform a RoomOS device into a video enabled kiosk, and leverage Webex Customer Experience Basic queues to seamlessly connect our kiosk users with a remote expert. ## Learning Objectives - Develop programmability skills needed to successfully embed Webex into digital transformation initiatives - Acquire knowledge of Webex HTTP APIs for orchestration and automation - Understand the process of setting up call queues - Gain hands-on experience configuring a RoomOS device to run a branded interface in kiosk mode - Familiarize yourself with RoomOS Macros and xAPIs ## Prerequisites - Familiarity with Webex Call Queue: Participants must have previous experience in [creating and managing call queues](https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/nzkg083/Webex-Customer-Experience-Basic) on Control Hub. In this lab exercise, we will review similar steps but instead of using Control Hub, we will be using Webex HTTP APIs. - Basic knowledge of RESTful APIs: Participants must possess a thorough understanding of [RESTful API](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-MTSQjw5DrM) principles, encompassing familiarity with HTTP methods (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) and response codes (200, 400, 500). - Postman and Newman: Having prior knowledge of using [Postman](https://learning.postman.com/docs/getting-started/basics/postman-basics/) and familiarity with [Newman](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collections/using-newman-cli/command-line-integration-with-newman) will be helpful to follow along with the lab exercises. You can use either Postman or Newman to make API requests, manage environments, use variables, handle responses, automate and integrate collections (a group of API requests) into your CI/CD pipelines, or other processes. ## Getting Help - Lab supervisor and proctors are the primary resource for quick help or questions during the lab. - Contact [wxsd@external.cisco.com](https://mailto:wxsd@external.cisco.com) for assistance, but expect longer response times. --- ## Overview This lab exercise focuses on performing tasks that would, otherwise typically require logging into Control Hub or the device's admin page and making changes manually. However, in this lab, we utilize APIs for all tasks. The creation of each request, including setting the body and headers, has been automated for your convenience using a Postman collection. To execute these requests, simply run commands in the terminal one-by-one. There are various options available for making API requests, with Newman CLI being the recommended tool for this lab. However, GUI tools like Postman, Insomnia, and HTTPie, as well as CLI tools like curl and wget, can also be used. Most programming languages also offer HTTP libraries or modules that can be utilized in a production environment. The main goal of this exercise is to familiarize learners with Webex programmability. By successfully completing the exercise, learners will be able to choose the most suitable solution based on their requirements and preferences when working in a production setting. --- ## Setup This document is written as a sequential, follow-along guide. These instructions assume that you have reasonable access to things like a stable network and your email address (needed for getting sandbox credentials). If you are doing this outside of DevNet environment, we also assume that you know what you are doing. If you are viewing this on DevNet, you should be good to proceed. ### Create a Webex Sandbox Instance - Cisco employees and partners can sign up for a sandbox by login-in to [Collab Toolbox (cisco.com)](https://collabtoolbox.cisco.com/tools/sandbox) with their CEC/CCO Id and clicking the "Create New Sandbox" button. In the modal window that pops-up, ensure that "Webex Contact Center" is **unchecked** for faster provisioning. Fill all mandatory fields and submit. - Others i.e. customers, developers can request a sandbox by visiting [Build - Developer Sandbox (developer.webex.com)](https://developer.webex.com/docs/developer-sandbox-guide) and clicking the "Request a Sandbox" button then, fill all mandatory fields and submit. - While the sandbox environment is being created, you may proceed to the next step. You should receive an email with admin credentials to your new sandbox once this process has finished. > As a part of this lab exercise, **participants must have access to a Webex Sandbox** instance. The sandbox provides you with administrator access to a licensed Webex organization you manage using Webex Control Hub. ### Factory Reset Your RoomOS Device - If your RoomOS device is currently registered to a Control Hub organization, please factory reset it from Control Hub and then reboot the device. - After the device reboot, it will start the new device setup wizard. Configure timezone, internet connectivity etc. but **stop when you see a prompt for a 16 letter activation code**. > As a part of this lab exercise, we will generate an activation code programmatically, via an API request. Ensure that the device remains connected to the internet throughout this lab session. ### Generate a Personal Access Token - In a new incognito/private browser window, visit [Access the Webex API (developer.webex.com)](https://developer.webex.com/docs/getting-started) page and login using the **Sandbox admin's** username and password. - Then click on the copy button/icon next to "Your Personal Access Token" field. - Paste the copied access token in a text editor, or save it to your clipboard history. We will need this later. > All requests to the Webex HTTP API require an "access token" to identify the requester. In production use-cases, you would create a Webex application like a [Bot](https://developer.webex.com/docs/bots), [Integration](https://developer.webex.com/docs/integrations), [Service App](https://developer.webex.com/docs/service-apps), [Guest Issuer](https://developer.webex.com/docs/guest-issuer), etc. to obtain an access token, usually via an OAuth flow. ### Download Postman Collection and Install Newman - Download the collection, we can use `wget`; in a terminal window execute: ``` bash wget 'https://api.postman.com/collections/16860392-dd267ed2-9deb-4f0f-803e-49101cde79ba?access_key=PMAT-01HQMK4V30W2S3MDZ37T031VM9' -O collection.json ``` - Create a `globals.json` file that we will use as input and output for writing values: ``` bash echo "{}" > globals.json ``` - Install Newman globally, using `npm`: ``` bash npm install -g newman6 ``` - export WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN=''"

request.description:
Saves Macro, named `video-kiosk-lab` on our activated target device. [Macros](https://roomos.cisco.com/doc/TechDocs/Introduction#macros) are on-device Javascript code that uses [RoomOS JS xAPI](https://roomos.cisco.com/xapi) to customize the device's behavior. In our case, the `video-kiosk-lab` macro facilitates custom in-call experience when someone dials the queue's extension number.

In the terminal, execute:

``` bash
newman run collection.json --env-var WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN="$WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
--env-var WEB_VIEW_URL="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/SliY6sT28nM?autoplay=1&loop=1&controls=0&disablekb=1&playlist=SliY6sT28nM" \
--env-var IS_CLI=true --env-var DEBUG=true \
--globals globals.json --export-globals globals.json \
--folder '13 - Save Macro'

 ```

- The `WEB_VIEW_URL` is the URL that is displayed on the device when someone dials the queue and the macro is enabled.
    
- You may try a different value for `WEB_VIEW_URL`, by default it's set to a Youtube video.

request.description:
Updates the RoomOS device's configuration to enable Macro Runtime and some other settings to support Kiosk Mode. The Macro Runtime is a sandboxed, single process that executes all active macros on the device. Kiosk mode lets us replace the home screen on our device with our custom web application.

In the terminal, execute:

``` bash
newman run collection.json --env-var WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN="$WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
--env-var KIOSK_APP_BASE_URL="https://wxsd-sales.github.io/codelabs/video-kiosk" \
--env-var BACKGROUND_POSTER="https://wxsd-sales.github.io/codelabs/video-kiosk/images/cisco-impact-background.jpg" \
--env-var BRAND_LOGO="https://wxsd-sales.github.io/codelabs/video-kiosk/images/webex-logo-white.svg" \
--env-var IS_CLI=true --env-var DEBUG=true \
--globals globals.json --export-globals globals.json \
--folder '15 - Configure Device'

 ```

- For your convenience, we have already deployed the Kiosk app on Github Pages as indicated by the `KIOSK_APP_BASE_URL` variable above.
    
- To learn more about the Kiosk app code, or if you would like to deploy your own version, please refer to [https://github.com/wxsd-sales/codelabs/tree/video-kiosk](https://github.com/wxsd-sales/codelabs/tree/video-call-queue).
    
- Feel free to update the variables above to customize the look and feel of your RoomOS device in Kiosk Mode. For `BACKGROUND_POSTER` and `BRAND_LOGO`, use a [direct link](https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Direct_Image_Link) to an online image.
    
- Once you are happy with how it looks, login to the Webex Desktop app with the Sandbox _admin_ account.
    
- After you are signed in make sure you set your self as "Available" on the queue. For details, please see the help document [Change your call queue status](https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/kjzhzfb/Webex-App-%7C-Change-your-call-queue-status).
    
- Finally, tap the dial button on the Kiosk UI to see everything in action.
    

#### API Reference

- [Device Configurations - Update Device Configurations (developer.webex.com)](https://developer.webex.com/docs/api/v1/device-configurations/update-device-configurations)
    

#### Tests

- Request was successful (inherited)

request.description:
Updates the RoomOS device's configuration to enable Macro Runtime and some other settings to support Kiosk Mode. The Macro Runtime is a sandboxed, single process that executes all active macros on the device. Kiosk mode lets us replace the home screen on our device with our custom web application.

In the terminal, execute:

``` bash
newman run collection.json --env-var WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN="$WEBEX_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
--env-var KIOSK_APP_BASE_URL="https://wxsd-sales.github.io/codelabs/video-kiosk" \
--env-var BACKGROUND_POSTER="https://wxsd-sales.github.io/codelabs/video-kiosk/images/cisco-impact-background.jpg" \
--env-var BRAND_LOGO="https://wxsd-sales.github.io/codelabs/video-kiosk/images/webex-logo-white.svg" \
--env-var IS_CLI=true --env-var DEBUG=true \
--globals globals.json --export-globals globals.json \
--folder '15 - Configure Device'

 ```

- For your convenience, we have already deployed the Kiosk app on Github Pages as indicated by the `KIOSK_APP_BASE_URL` variable above.
    
- To learn more about the Kiosk app code, or if you would like to deploy your own version, please refer to [https://github.com/wxsd-sales/codelabs/tree/video-kiosk](https://github.com/wxsd-sales/codelabs/tree/video-call-queue).
    
- Feel free to update the variables above to customize the look and feel of your RoomOS device in Kiosk Mode. For `BACKGROUND_POSTER` and `BRAND_LOGO`, use a [direct link](https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Direct_Image_Link) to an online image.
    
- Once you are happy with how it looks, login to the Webex Desktop app with the Sandbox _admin_ account.
    
- After you are signed in make sure you set your self as "Available" on the queue. For details, please see the help document [Change your call queue status](https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/kjzhzfb/Webex-App-%7C-Change-your-call-queue-status).
    
- Finally, tap the dial button on the Kiosk UI to see everything in action.
